subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session defaults continue to override later `tools.exec` config, or should operator config act as an authoritative security floor that clears or dominates stored exec fields after config changes?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests intentionally preserve `/exec` session defaults, while the report identifies a real security-policy shadowing risk; automation should not choose that boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Make operator policy authoritative
options.body: Treat global or per-agent exec config as the security floor and add reset/migration coverage for existing persisted session exec fields.

options.title: Keep session defaults as documented
options.body: Preserve current `/exec` precedence but add stronger diagnostics and operator reset guidance so stale session policy is visible and recoverable.

options.title: Add explicit reset controls first
options.body: Leave precedence unchanged initially and implement a narrow operator-facing session exec reset path before considering resolver changes.

recommendation.title: Make operator policy authoritative
recommendation.body: Treat global or per-agent exec config as the security floor and add reset/migration coverage for existing persisted session exec fields.

likelyOwner.reason: This route is closest to the original `/exec` session override behavior and its focused resolver coverage.
